## Tests to write:

### 1. src/test/utils.test.ts — cn() utility
- merges class names correctly
- handles conditional classes
- handles undefined/null/false values
- deduplicates conflicting tailwind classes (e.g. text-red-500 overridden by text-blue-500)

### 2. src/test/csvExport.test.ts — exportToCSV()
Mock URL.createObjectURL, URL.revokeObjectURL, and document.createElement('a').click.
Test:
- returns early if data is empty
- builds correct CSV header row from object keys
- quotes all values
- escapes double quotes inside values (replace " with "")
- handles null/undefined values as empty string
- downloads with correct filename containing today's date

### 3. src/test/stageTracker.test.ts — pure logic + STAGE_ORDER constants
- STAGE_ORDER has exactly 5 stages in correct order: applied, screened, interview, offer, hired
- "rejected" is NOT in STAGE_ORDER
- HiringStage type covers all 6 values
- Stage index calculations: applied=0, screened=1, interview=2, offer=3, hired=4
- Stage summary computation: given an array of CandidateStage records, counts each stage correctly
- useStageSummary handles empty stages array (all counts = 0)

### 4. src/test/stageFilter.test.ts — the stage filter logic we added to JobDetailView
This is pure logic extracted for testing. Write pure functions that mirror the logic:

```typescript
// The filter logic (extracted from JobDetailView)
type HiringStage = "applied"|"screened"|"interview"|"offer"|"hired"|"rejected";
interface Result { resume_id: string; pending?: boolean; overall_score: number; }
interface StageEntry { resume_id: string; stage: HiringStage; }

function filterByStage(results: Result[], stageMap: Map<string, StageEntry>, stageFilter: HiringStage | null) {
  return results.filter(r => {
    if (!stageFilter) return true;
    const candidateStage = stageMap.get(r.resume_id)?.stage ?? "applied";
    return candidateStage === stageFilter;
  });
}

function computeStageCounts(results: Result[], stageMap: Map<string, StageEntry>, dismissed: Set<string>) {
  const stages = ["applied","screened","interview","offer","hired","rejected"] as const;
  const nonArchived = results.filter(r => !dismissed.has(r.resume_id) && !r.pending);
  return stages.reduce((acc, stage) => {
    acc[stage] = nonArchived.filter(r => (stageMap.get(r.resume_id)?.stage ?? "applied") === stage).length;
    return acc;
  }, {} as Record<string, number>);
}
```

Test:
- filterByStage returns all results when stageFilter is null
- filterByStage returns only matching results for a given stage
- filterByStage treats candidates with no stageMap entry as "applied"
- filterByStage correctly filters by "rejected"
- computeStageCounts counts un-staged candidates as "applied"
- computeStageCounts excludes dismissed candidates
- computeStageCounts excludes pending candidates
- computeStageCounts returns 0 for stages with no candidates

### 5. src/test/seoCanonical.test.ts — canonical URL logic (bug we fixed)
Extract and test the fixed canonical URL logic:

```typescript
function buildCanonical(
  pageCanonical: string | undefined,
  globalCanonical: string | undefined,
  pathname: string
): string {
  const canonicalBase = (globalCanonical || "").replace(/\/$/, "");
  return pageCanonical || (canonicalBase ? `${canonicalBase}${pathname}` : "");
}
```

Test:
- returns per-page canonical as-is (does NOT append pathname)
- appends pathname to global canonical base URL
- handles trailing slash on global canonical URL
- returns empty string when both are empty/undefined
- handles root pathname "/"
- handles nested pathname "/settings/billing"
- per-page canonical takes priority over global + pathname

### 6. src/test/contactExtraction.test.ts — contact field extraction from parsed_json
Extract and test the merging logic:

```typescript
function extractContact(parsed: any) {
  return {
    candidate_email: parsed?.email ?? parsed?.contact?.email ?? null,
    candidate_phone: parsed?.phone ?? parsed?.contact?.phone ?? null,
    candidate_location: parsed?.location ?? parsed?.contact?.location ?? null,
  };
}
```

Test:
- extracts email from top-level parsed.email
- extracts email from nested parsed.contact.email as fallback
- extracts phone from top-level parsed.phone
- extracts phone from nested parsed.contact.phone as fallback
- extracts location from top-level parsed.location
- returns null for all fields when parsed is null
- returns null for all fields when parsed is empty object {}
- top-level fields take priority over nested contact fields

### 7. src/test/StageTracker.test.tsx — StageTracker component rendering
Mock: vi.mock('date-fns', ...) if needed for format function

Test:
- renders all 5 stage labels: Applied, Screened, Interview, Offer, Hired
- renders reject (XCircle) button
- shows "Rejected" badge when currentStage is "rejected"
- calls onStageChange with correct stage when a dot is clicked
- calls onStageChange("rejected") when reject button is clicked
- shows formatted date when updatedAt is provided
- disabled prop prevents button interactions

- Run npm run test after writing all tests
- Fix any import or type errors
- All tests must pass
- Do NOT modify any source files — only create test files
